extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, action editors, and editors-in-chief of TMLR
extracted.subtask_short: TMLR submission guidelines and editorial policies
extracted.subtask_description: The Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) editorial policies page. Defines scope, dual-submission/originality rules, the open double-blind review process, evaluation criteria, certifications, ethics, conflicts of interest, authorship criteria, and misconduct handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: papers contributing to principles of learning in brains or machines
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR's objective is to publish original papers that contribute to the understanding of the computational and mathematical principles that enable intelligence through learning, be it in brains or in machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMLR invites: papers with new algorithms with sound empirical validation, optionally with justification of theoretical, psychological, or biological nature; experimental and/or theoretical studies yielding new insight into the design and behavior of learning in intelligent systems; accounts of applications of existing techniques that shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of the methods; formalization of new learning tasks and methods for assessing performance on those tasks; development of new analytical frameworks that advance theoretical studies of practical learning methods; computational models of natural learning systems at the behavioral or neural level; reproducibility studies of previously published results or claims; new approaches for analysis, visualization, and understanding of artificial or biological learning systems; surveys that draw new connections, highlight trends, and suggest new problems in an area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original contributions only; no expanded conference versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike many other journals, TMLR only accepts original contributions that don't reuse the authors' own prior work. In particular, we do not accept submissions that are expanded versions of conference papers. There should not be any reuse of written text, figures or results between the submitted paper and any paper which has been published, accepted for publication, or submitted in parallel at another archival, peer-reviewed venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable for a submission to overlap with the author's previous work if it was shared at venues or tracks that are publicly declared, in writing, to be non-archival, such as workshops, or on preprint servers such as arXiv and bioRxiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open, double-blind review process
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR uses an open-reviewing, double-blind process. An open reviewing model, where papers, reviews, and discussion are visible to the public, provides several benefits, including transparency of the process, reviews which are higher-quality and more constructive, and easier communication between authors and reviewers. Since there is ample evidence that single-blind reviewing may lead to biased outcomes, we follow a double blind model where the identities of authors and invited reviewers are withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected not to take any actions that would violate this double blind state, e.g. searching for related presentations or arXiv preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action editor screening and reviewer assignment within a week
rubrics_metrics.description: An action editor will be assigned to the submission within a week. They will evaluate the submission, and may reject it immediately for reasons including (but not limited to): being out of scope, TMLR having insufficient reviewer expertise to adequately handle, being poor quality or unlikely to meet TMLR's acceptance criteria, or having format violations (contingent on Editor-in-Chief approval). Otherwise, the action editor will assign at least three qualified reviewers and the paper will become public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public may volunteer to review the paper; accepting such offers is up to the discretion of the action editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews kept independent until all are submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will be visible to the authors as they are submitted, but the reviews will not be visible to the public nor to the other reviewers until all the reviews are submitted in order to keep them independent. Authors may post rebuttals and update their papers in response to the reviews, and the reviewers and editor may privately discuss the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can respond to a review as soon as it is posted; recommended to wait until all 3 reviews are in before submitting a revised PDF. Reviewers will be able to submit their final recommendations once at least two weeks have elapsed after all 3 reviews became public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision categories: accept, accept with minor revision, reject
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion period ends when the action editor enters a decision for the paper, which is one of the following: Accept as is; Accept with minor revision; Reject: the author is notified of the rejection, and the action editor indicates whether they would be willing to consider a significantly revised version of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission remains publicly available on OpenReview and the authors are given the opportunity to reveal their identity. Doing so will preclude them from submitting a revised version of the manuscript to TMLR. Authors of a rejected submission may revise and resubmit their paper, but it will need to be entered as a new submission and a link provided to the previously rejected submission as well as a description of the changes made since.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion 1: claims supported by accurate, convincing, clear evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims made in the submission supported by accurate, convincing and clear evidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers that should not be accepted include papers that make bold statements unsupported by empirical or rigorous evidence, papers that aren't clearly written, papers that incorrectly claim novelty over existing published work, and papers that merely re-implement an idea that has already been reproduced before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion 2: at least some TMLR audience would be interested
rubrics_metrics.description: Would at least some individuals in TMLR's audience be interested in knowing the findings of this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should be accepted if they meet the criteria, even if the contribution or significance of the work is modest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modest contributions are acceptable; novelty is not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be accepted if they meet the criteria, even if the contribution or significance of the work is modest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit anti-pattern: rejecting solely on grounds of modest novelty or significance is not justified under TMLR criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Certification for exceptional, broadly significant work
rubrics_metrics.description: Outstanding Certification. The editorial board of TMLR jointly awards this certification to papers which are deemed to be exceptionally high quality and broadly significant for the field. The certification may be given well after the paper's initial publication in TMLR (a year or more), and is equivalent to a best paper award at a top-tier conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most prestigious certification; jointly approved by all editors-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured Certification for very high quality novel contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured Certification. This certification may be awarded to papers that are very high quality. These papers present significant contributions which are novel, clearly explained, and well supported with evidence, theory, or analysis. If this paper was submitted to a top-tier conference, it would likely be presented as an oral/spotlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominated by action editors, must be reviewed and approved by at least one editor-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility Certification with added value beyond verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility Certification. This is awarded to papers whose primary purpose is reproduction of other published work. Beyond simple verification, the paper must contribute significant added value through additional baselines, analysis, ablations, or insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Certification for exceptionally insightful surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey Certification. Papers that not only meet the criteria for acceptance but also provide an exceptionally thorough or insightful survey of the topic or approach may be awarded this certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access policy: free public access, no fees
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR makes all published content immediately available to the public free of charge. TMLR imposes no fees or payments to authors, reviewers, action editors, or editors-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM use policy: assistive only, authors responsible, LLMs not authors
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs may be used as general-purpose assistive tools. Whichever tools are used, authors are fully responsible for content on which they are listed as (co-) authors. This includes, but is not limited to, content generated by LLMs that could be construed as plagiarism or scientific misconduct (e.g., fabrication of facts). Low-quality contributions (be they submissions or reviews) that appear to be largely LLM-generated will be closely examined for evidence of the issues mentioned previously, such as scientific misconduct. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will periodically revise this policy as new information about the use of LLMs in the scientific process becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest: domain and personal conflicts in OpenReview
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and co-authors will use their OpenReview profile to identify domain and personal conflicts. Domain conflicts, entered in Education & Career History, are used to identify institutions with which you have a conflict of interest from (at least) the last three years. Be judicious with domain conflicts and only use them if you have a genuine conflict. It is forbidden to state a false conflict in order to block potentially negative reviewers from an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For current or recent collaborations, including internships, you should generally use personal conflicts, which are recorded in the Advisors, Relations & Conflicts section. The following constitutes a personal conflict: Family or close personal relationship; Ph.D. advisee/advisor relationship; Current, frequent, or recent collaboration (where recent means within the past three years). If an action editor or editor-in-chief has reason to doubt the validity of such a conflict, the EiCs may confidentially inquire into its nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: EiC-authored submissions handled by non-conflicting AE
rubrics_metrics.description: If a TMLR Editor-in-chief submits a paper to the journal, the other editor(s)-in-chief will choose an action editor that is not in conflict with any of the editors-in-chief to oversee the review. If a TMLR action editor submits a paper, it will be assigned to a different, non-conflicting action editor to oversee the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship requires substantial contribution, drafting role, full responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals should be listed as authors on a TMLR submission if and only if they satisfy all of the following criteria: They have made a substantial intellectual contribution to the work described in the submission. This may include, but is not limited to: conception, design, or analysis of the work. They have contributed to drafting or revising the submission. They take full responsibility for all content in the final published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals listed as authors testify: they are aware the submission has been submitted; they agree to be held responsible and accountable for issues related to correctness or integrity; to the best of their knowledge, the work submitted is original, all individuals who satisfy the authorship criteria are listed as authors, and the submission is an honest representation of the underlying work. All authors must be listed on OpenReview, with active OpenReview profiles, at the time of submission and throughout the review process. There are no exceptions to this policy. TMLR gives no prescription on how to order authors. Adapted from similar policies of ACM and IEEE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical publishing: TMLR follows COPE guidelines for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of author, reviewer, or editor misconduct should be sent to the editors-in-chief, except that if the allegations concern an EiC, the allegations may be sent directly to the personal emails of the non-accused subset of the EiCs. To handle an allegation or discovery of misconduct, TMLR follows the Committee on Publishing Ethics's (COPE) guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination of misconduct may result in TMLR contacting the author institutions, funding agencies, and/or potential victims. At the discretion of the Editors-in-Chief, additional actions may be taken, including issuing an informal or formal warning to the offender and barring them from submitting a manuscript to TMLR for a fixed duration. Covered cases include: suspected plagiarism in submitted/published manuscripts; suspected redundant publication; suspected fabricated data; reviewer suspected to have appropriated an author's ideas or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics guidelines and Broader Impact for potentially harmful work
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Ethics Guidelines describe TMLR's ethical principles and establish common ground for editors, reviewers, and authors to evaluate the potential for harm of a proposed work. Submissions which describe work with the potential for harm should clearly describe the risks and mitigations in an (otherwise optional) Broader Impact Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In situations where a reviewer with ethics expertise is required to evaluate the impact and potential for harm, or where the action editor suspects that no statement would make the work ethically acceptable, reach out to the Editors-in-Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and post-publication changes follow COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editors-in-Chief may also decide to withdraw a submission or retract an accepted paper if it is found to contain unethical research, any plagiarized content (including figures), or findings that are erroneous (due to misconduct or honest error). By default, TMLR follows COPE guidelines (e.g., for adding or removing authors, or retracting a paper). In the event that TMLR retracts a publication... a Notice of Retraction will be attached to the paper on OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case of post-publication edits or corrections, the EiCs may involve the paper's Action Editor to judge the proposed edits, including their correctness and/or appropriateness (checking, e.g., if the paper instead ought be retracted, or if the changes should be included in a separate and subsequent publication). Any significant changes should be documented in a section at the end of the paper titled 'Post-Publication Changes.' In all cases the paper's full revision history will remain visible on OpenReview, and the Editors in Chief will post a public comment on the OpenReview page upon update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and retraction handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may decide to withdraw their submission before a decision has been entered, or they may decide to retract their submission after acceptance. In the former case, authors may trigger the withdrawal themselves, through OpenReview. The author will need to enter a reason for the withdrawal, and the submission will remain on OpenReview but its status will be explicitly marked as withdrawn. If an author decides to retract their paper after it is accepted, they will need to enter a retraction statement in OpenReview. The retraction statement will be reviewed by the Editors-in-Chief and all authors will be contacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors will be given the option to reveal their identity, otherwise the withdrawn submission will remain public but anonymous. Once retraction is confirmed, the paper will remain on OpenReview but its status will be marked as retracted.
